mentions.description: This platform lets people crowdfund independent plastic chemical lab testing of specific food products they buy. Users find or suggest a product, contribute to its testing fund, and receive full lab results when testing completes, with automatic refunds if a product's goal isn't reached within 365 days. All results are published publicly. Testing uses ISO 17025-accredited methodology (the same as PlasticList.org), samples up to three separate production lots per product when possible, detects down to parts-per-billion, and follows an open protocol.
mentions.problem: People have no way to get independent lab testing for plastic chemicals and endocrine disruptors in the specific food products they actually buy.
mentions.audience: Consumers and shoppers who want to know about plastic chemical contamination in the specific foods they buy, plus anyone curious enough to propose and fund tests of particular products.

mentions.name: Laboratory.love
mentions.description: This platform lets users crowdfund independent lab testing of the consumer products they buy, focused on detecting endocrine disruptors (BPA/BPS/BPF and phthalates) in foods. Users find or suggest a product, contribute to its testing fund, and get full lab results published publicly; products that don't reach their funding goal within 365 days are automatically refunded. Testing uses ISO 17025-accredited methodology across three production lots per product with parts-per-billion detection, published results tables calculate EFSA Tolerable Daily Intake percentages for toddlers and adults, and monthly subscriptions pool funds toward the leading unfunded product. The stated goal is making supply chains transparent so cleaner ones win.
mentions.problem: Plastic chemicals were found in 86% of tested foods (including 100% of baby foods) in 2024, while FDA limits for BPA remain roughly 100× higher than the EU's new standard, leaving consumers without data on what's in the products they buy.
mentions.audience: Consumers who want real data on chemical contamination in products they buy, including parents concerned about food safety.

mentions.description: A crowdfunding platform for independent, ISO 17025-accredited lab testing of consumer products for plastic chemicals such as BPA/BPS/BPF and phthalates. Users find or suggest a product, contribute to its testing fund (automatically refunded if the goal isn't reached within 365 days), and receive full lab results when testing completes. Each product is tested in triplicate across three separate production lots with detection down to parts-per-billion, using an open protocol, and all results are published publicly so consumers get real data and markets can shift toward cleaner supply chains.
mentions.problem: Plastic chemicals were found in 86% of foods tested by PlasticList, including 100% of baby foods, while regulatory limits lag far behind (the EU lowered its BPA limit 20,000× while the FDA allows levels ~100× higher), leaving consumers without trustworthy chemical-contamination data for the products they buy.
mentions.audience: Consumers who want independent lab data on the products they actually buy, from everyday groceries to kids' snacks.

Users find or suggest a product, contribute to its testing fund, and get detailed lab results when testing completes; campaigns that miss their funding goal within 365 days are automatically refunded. Testing uses ISO 17025-accredited labs, three samples from different production lots, and detection down to parts per billion under a public testing protocol following PlasticList.org's methodology, with all results published openly so consumer data creates market pressure for cleaner supply chains.
mentions.problem: Food products widely contain plastic chemicals—PlasticList found 86% of tested products (including 100% of baby food) contain plastic chemicals, and the FDA allows BPA levels 100x higher than what Europe considers safe—leaving consumers without independent testing data for the specific products they buy.
